claims.text: Bun maintainers said Bun 1.0 was "stable and production-ready" for macOS and Linux, while Windows was still "highly experimental."

evidence_passages.text: Maintainers explicitly said on September 8, 2023 that Bun 1.0 was "stable and production-ready" for macOS and Linux, while Windows was still "highly experimental" and had the package manager, test runner, and bundler disabled. https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.0

claims.text: Bun's own documentation and release notes say Node.js compatibility is still incomplete.

evidence_passages.text: Maintainers also still say compatibility is incomplete: the docs call Node.js compatibility an "ongoing effort," and the Bun 1.4 release notes say Bun is "not 100% compatible with Node.js yet." https://bun.sh/docs, https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4, https://bun.com/docs/runtime/nodejs-compat

claims.text: Bun maintainers publicly point to named production use cases, including Claude Code, Midjourney image notifications, and Railway Functions.
acceptable_patterns: Claude Code ships as a Bun executable
Midjourney sends every image notification through Bun
Railway built its Functions product on Bun

evidence_passages.text: Maintainers provide concrete production-use claims on the Bun homepage: it says Claude Code ships as a Bun executable, Midjourney sends every image notification through Bun’s WebSocket server, and Railway built its Functions product on Bun. https://bun.com/

claims.text: Anthropic independently said Bun had been "key" to scaling Claude Code's infrastructure.
acceptable_patterns: Bun had been "key" to scaling Claude Code’s infrastructure

evidence_passages.text: Anthropic independently said on December 3, 2025 that Bun had been "key" to scaling Claude Code’s infrastructure and that Anthropic was acquiring Bun. https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-acquires-bun-as-claude-code-reaches-usd1b-milestone

claims.text: Bun's own issue tracker includes production-like reports of memory growth and crashes under Bun workloads.
acceptable_patterns: RSS at 2\.46 GB followed by a segmentation fault
growing from about 50 MB to 170 MB

evidence_passages.text: User reports with concrete symptoms exist in Bun’s own tracker: An Express app in Docker was reported as crashing 4 GB pods from memory growth in production on Bun 1.2.14. https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/19930

A large `fetch` workload on Bun 1.2.18 was reported with RSS at 2.46 GB followed by a segmentation fault, and Bun’s own crash message said this indicated a bug in Bun. https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/20912

A Mongoose production build on Bun was reported as growing from about 50 MB to 170 MB in 12 hours, and another container from 300 MB to 1.5 GB in a day, even while idle, leading to container death. https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/25948

claims.text: Some users reported mixed migration outcomes and said they still kept Node in production or as a fallback because of Bun bugs.
acceptable_patterns: need to use Node "because of a bug"

evidence_passages.text: There are also user reports of mixed migration outcomes: one user said they migrated a monorepo with 300+ packages and about 100,000 lines of code, but hit missing APIs, memory-corruption suspicions, packaging problems, and ended up saying they still used Node "in production." https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/discussions/3955
Another user said they keep a wrapper because there are still occasions where they need to use Node "because of a bug." https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/discussions/17485

rejected_claims.text: Bun is broadly proven everywhere in production.
rejected_claims.reason: Overly broad; the supplied evidence shows some successful production use, not universal readiness.
Contradicted by supplied evidence about named production users and Anthropic's statement.

rejected_claims.text: GitHub issues show how common Bun production failures are.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported; the supplied evidence explicitly says issue reports do not establish prevalence.
Contradicted by Bun's own docs and release notes saying compatibility is ongoing and not 100% yet.

rejected_claims.text: Bun 1.4 fixed all reliability and memory problems.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported and time-unstable; the evidence mentions remediation work and improvements, not complete resolution.
